what: Offline: which service am I on?
title: Azure
text: cloud.provider "azure" VM’s DMI data says (Azure sets fixed chassis asset tag), Hyper-V combined Azure guest agent (/var/lib/waagent Linux, C:/WindowsAzure Windows), one Azure services sets environment variables. cloud.azure.platform names service: cloud.azure.service holds service’s non-secret identifiers, e.g. App Service site instance Batch pool, node, job task.

title: Azure
text: f$cloud$azure adds VM name, resource group, subscription, scale set, spot priority eviction policy, image, tags IP addresses. Tags whose name looks like secret redacted, like environment variables. pod, metadata describes node VM, pod: summary says node make clear.

what: What zufax does and does not do
title: Azure
text: request made without cloud = TRUE (options(zufax.cloud = TRUE)), none Azure: offline check comes first. Exactly one URL can requested: http://169.254.169.254/metadata/instance?api-version=2021-02-01. managed identity endpoints (/metadata/identity/...) hand access tokens refused connection made. request bypasses configured proxy, times 1 second made per session, failures included. refresh = TRUE tries . IMDS blocked (network policies, App Service, Container Apps), facts unavailable reason facts_df(). Parsing response needs jsonlite package.

title: Installed packages
text: zufax never runs pip, conda, brew apt, never starts Python inside R. Python found RETICULATE_PYTHON, VIRTUAL_ENV, CONDA_PREFIX PATH (py launcher Windows).

what: How many cores, how much memory?
title: Getting started with zufax
text: parallel::detectCores() counts host’s CPUs. Inside container process usually allowed far fewer. effective_cores() takes smallest : host’s logical CPUs, process’s CPU affinity, cgroup’s cpuset, cgroup’s CPU quota, rounded (1.5-core quota can keep 2 threads busy). effective_memory() smaller host memory cgroup memory limit. effective_memory("available") can still allocated, counting reclaimable page cache free. Use size worker pools: ignore settings mc.cores MC_CORES purpose: describe resources, policy. parallelly::availableCores() combines .
code: effective_cores() #> [1] 4 effective_memory() #> [1] 16760340480 future::plan(future::multisession, workers = effective_cores()) data.table::setDTthreads(effective_cores()) options(mc.cores = effective_cores())

title: Getting started with zufax
text: zufax pod limited 2 CPUs 1 GiB node 8 CPUs 32 GiB. limits set pod’s cgroup, parent container’s: detectCores() say 8. CPU facts show 2 comes : memory, container used 300 MiB, 100 MiB inactive page cache kernel can reclaim. Like kubelet, zufax counts remaining 200 MiB working set, leaving 824 MiB available. Kubernetes facts come environment files kubelet mounts. node name, pod IP resources visible Downward API: expose environment variables (zufax looks NODE_NAME, POD_IP, POD_UID, POD_NAME, CPU_LIMIT, MEMORY_LIMIT, CPU_REQUEST MEMORY_REQUEST, set options(zufax.k8s.env = )) mount labels annotations /etc/podinfo (set options(zufax.k8s.podinfo = )). zufax never reads service account token.
code: facts() #> <zufax facts> #> os       Ubuntu 22.04 #> runs in  Kubernetes pod default/web-6b8f9-2xkqz, containerd container #> runs on  vm (unknown) #> cpu      host 8 | effective 2 #> memory   host 32G | limit 1G | available 824M #> Use facts_df() for every fact with its status and source. str(facts()$cpu[c("host", "affinity", "cgroup", "effective")]) #> List of 4 #>  $ host     :List of 3 #>   ..$ logical : int 8 #>   ..$ physical: int 4 #>   ..$ sockets : int 1 #>  $ affinity : int 8 #>  $ cgroup   :List of 3 #>   ..$ quota : num 2 #>   ..$ cpuset: int 8 #>   ..$ weight: num 79 #>  $ effective: int 2

title: zufax 0.1.0
text: Initial CRAN submission. effective_cores() effective_memory() return CPU cores memory process can actually use, taking cgroup v1/v2 limits, cpusets CPU affinity account. facts(), fact() facts_df() provide lazy, cached snapshot facts per-fact status source. Resolver errors never escape unless strict = TRUE. Facts describe OS (os.*), CPU, memory cgroups, process runs: bare metal VM (virtualization.*, including WSL), container (container.*), Kubernetes pod (k8s.*, including Downward API) cloud provider (cloud.provider). facts_json() writes facts JSON, optionally status source; print() facts() snapshot shows short summary process runs can use. Runtime facts describe R (version, BLAS/LAPACK, library paths, repositories credentials removed, renv, thread settings), process (pid, user, uid, privileges) Python (interpreter, version, venv/uv/conda/system, site-packages) without starting Python inside R. env.vars reports environment variables secrets redacted default (zufax.redact, zufax.redact_allowlist); env.proxies disk.tmpdir.* describe proxies temporary directory. macOS Windows supported host facts: OS, CPU model topology, memory, boot time, virtualization (Azure Windows), temporary directory Python discovery (py launcher, per-user installs). Azure: cloud.azure.platform tells VM, AKS, App Service, Functions, Container Apps, Batch, Azure ML Databricks apart without network access. facts(cloud = TRUE) instance metadata service adds region, zone, VM size id, resource group, subscription, spot settings, image, tags (redacted) IP addresses. Requests go instance metadata endpoint, time 1 second made per session. opt-packages namespace lists installed system packages (dpkg, rpm, apk, pacman, Homebrew, Windows), R packages Python packages, read package databases rather running pip package managers possible. facts() stays quiet: warnings raised resolving facts muffled, os.timezone avoids slow Sys.timezone() lookup time zone can read TZ /etc/localtime. cgroup v2 pressure stall information (memory.cgroup.pressure, cpu.cgroup.pressure) OOM kill counts (memory.cgroup.oom_kills); usage(extra = "pressure") adds usage sample, print() notes OOM kills tempdir() tmpfs containers. runtime.r.connections reports free R connection slots (parallel worker needs one) runtime.rlimit.nofile open-files limit. usage() usage_line() report current process container CPU memory use cheaply enough call every log line.
